title: galium trifidum subsp. tinctorium
intro: Galium trifidum subsp. tinctorium, commonly known as Wild Madder, is a plant species belonging to the Rubiaceae family, characterized by its reddish-pink flowers and edible roots. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including the treatment of fever, diarrhea, and skin conditions, due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Wild Madder include its ability to calm the nervous system, reduce pain and inflammation, and promote wound healing. The bioactive constituents of the plant include alkaloids, glycosides, and phenolic compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
